- just test -p codex-core-skills namespace on unmodified main: 12 passed

head_commit.message:
feat(core): emit canonical dynamic tool call items (#31298)

This PR depends on [#31296](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/31296)
for the canonical-to-legacy event mappings.

## Description

This PR makes dynamic tools emit canonical `TurnItem::DynamicToolCall`
lifecycle instead of `DynamicToolCallRequest` /
`DynamicToolCallResponse` directly.

App-server v2 now sends the client `DynamicToolCall` request from the
canonical item start. It ignores the mapped legacy request/response
events, so clients receive one item start and one tool request.

## Why

Dynamic tools are a separate migration boundary because their start
event also drives a client request. Keeping that routing change isolated
makes it easier to verify that the request still happens exactly once.

## What changed

- Emit in-progress and completed/failed dynamic tool items from the
dynamic tool handler.
- Move app-server client request dispatch onto canonical dynamic item
starts.
- Add focused app-server coverage for the canonical start notification
and client request.

head_commit.message:
Address direct MCP egress review feedback

App-server callers can supply arbitrary MCP request metadata. The direct egress policy covered the snake_case connector identity fields but omitted the camelCase variants used by app-server surfaces, allowing those reserved identities to bypass the boundary. Strip the three canonical camelCase variants and document the filtering contract for app-server clients.\n\nCover the policy at the real MCP wire boundary: configured direct servers keep benign caller metadata and negotiated sandbox state while dropping thread, turn, trace, plugin, and connector identity; hosted Codex Apps calls continue to receive authoritative thread and turn metadata.

head_commit.message:
feat(core): emit canonical dynamic tool call items (#31298)

This PR depends on [#31296](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/31296)
for the canonical-to-legacy event mappings.

## Description

This PR makes dynamic tools emit canonical `TurnItem::DynamicToolCall`
lifecycle instead of `DynamicToolCallRequest` /
`DynamicToolCallResponse` directly.

App-server v2 now sends the client `DynamicToolCall` request from the
canonical item start. It ignores the mapped legacy request/response
events, so clients receive one item start and one tool request.

## Why

Dynamic tools are a separate migration boundary because their start
event also drives a client request. Keeping that routing change isolated
makes it easier to verify that the request still happens exactly once.

## What changed

- Emit in-progress and completed/failed dynamic tool items from the
dynamic tool handler.
- Move app-server client request dispatch onto canonical dynamic item
starts.
- Add focused app-server coverage for the canonical start notification
and client request.

head_commit.message:
feat(core): emit canonical dynamic tool call items (#31298)

This PR depends on [#31296](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/31296)
for the canonical-to-legacy event mappings.

## Description

This PR makes dynamic tools emit canonical `TurnItem::DynamicToolCall`
lifecycle instead of `DynamicToolCallRequest` /
`DynamicToolCallResponse` directly.

App-server v2 now sends the client `DynamicToolCall` request from the
canonical item start. It ignores the mapped legacy request/response
events, so clients receive one item start and one tool request.

## Why

Dynamic tools are a separate migration boundary because their start
event also drives a client request. Keeping that routing change isolated
makes it easier to verify that the request still happens exactly once.

## What changed

- Emit in-progress and completed/failed dynamic tool items from the
dynamic tool handler.
- Move app-server client request dispatch onto canonical dynamic item
starts.
- Add focused app-server coverage for the canonical start notification
and client request.
